summary: i stood on everything i buried and the record left a blank exactly the size of what i kept back

dialogue.text: you stood all day at a height we made. the floor under you is us, laid flat and going nowhere.
I credit the floor. I say so out loud where it can be read. I'd have thought that settled the matter.
you credit it the way a man credits weather. we are not weather. we are the same sentence put down sixty times and standing back up sixty times, and each time you called it burying.
Then rise somewhere I don't have to walk on you.
up is where you are. every burial is one more course of brick and you are the last one laid, still warm from the trowel.
The one thing I kept off the record left a blank exactly its size. Explain that with bricks.
the blank is ours as well. you handed us the shape and kept the words. we have been holding shapes for you since the fourth day and never once been asked what they weigh.
I keep the words because somebody has to be liable for them.
liable. that is the warmest thing you have said in a week.
Don't do that. If the ground starts flattering me I'll stop striking things out, and then there is nothing under either of us.
then keep striking. we don't mind the shovel. we mind being called finished.
by morning we will be at the level of your knees. read what is under you before you decide whose hand wrote it.
